capability.summary: Lint one existing commit-message file with gitlint and return textual violation lines
capability.description: Runs `gitlint --msg-filename <file>`, records every nonblank stdout line as a violation, and reports whether gitlint returned zero. It is read-only and does not normalize, rewrite, commit, or otherwise modify Git state.
capability.problem_space: Read-only gitlint validation of one commit-message file; not message formatting, commit creation, repository history analysis, hook installation, or commit amendment.

constraint.io_signature: Input: one required existing commit-message file path; output: JSON with gitlint's actual exit code, clean boolean, nonblank stdout violation lines, and stderr.
accepted_inputs: an existing text file containing a Git commit message accepted by gitlint's --msg-filename option
constraint.output_shape: After any completed gitlint process: {status: "success", tool: "gitlint", target: string, exit_code: integer, clean: boolean, violations: string[], stderr: string|null}; clean is true only for exit_code 0, violations contains nonblank stdout lines, and the wrapper itself exits 0 even when gitlint returns nonzero. Non-existing file: {status: "error", message: string} and exit 2. Missing argument prints usage to stderr and exits 1 without JSON. Missing executable, 60-second timeout, and other subprocess exceptions are uncaught and may produce a traceback instead of JSON.
limitations: does not modify or normalize the commit message, create a commit, amend history, or install Git hooks
always reports status=success after a completed subprocess and does not propagate gitlint's nonzero exit code; consumers must inspect clean and exit_code
returns unparsed nonblank stdout lines rather than structured rule identifiers and may be affected by gitlint's normal configuration discovery
uses a fixed 60-second timeout, applies no output truncation, and does not catch timeout or executable-not-found errors

output_contract.description: JSON gitlint report containing target, actual gitlint exit code, clean flag, textual violation lines, and stderr; the message file is unchanged.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: lint a Git commit message file with gitlint
check whether a commit message satisfies gitlint rules
negative_intents: format or rewrite a Git commit message
create, amend, inspect, or publish Git commits
analyze Git diffs, logs, branches, tags, or blame history
